PENDULUM_SQUAT.name: Pendulum Squat
technique: Place feet low on platform at shoulder width
Unrack and descend slowly (3 seconds)
Drive knees forward over toes as deep as possible
mistakes: Locking knees at the top (removes tension)
PENDULUM_SQUAT.visualization: The Piston Cue: Imagine your femurs are pistons compressing a giant spring.
PENDULUM_SQUAT.proTip: By not locking out, you induce vascular occlusion, forcing Type II fibers to activate earlier.

LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.name: Low Incline DB Press
technique: Set bench to 15-30°
Retract scapula slightly into the bench
Press up and slightly inward, do not touch weights
LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.visualization: Bicep to Pec: Don't push up, try to touch your inner bicep to your pectorals.
LOW_INC_DB_PRESS.proTip: A 15° incline aligns perfectly with the clavicular fibers without front delt dominance.

HIGH_INC_SMITH.name: High Incline Smith Press
technique: Set bench to 45°
Lower bar toward the collarbone
Pause briefly on the chest
mistakes: Lowering to the nipple line (too low for 45°)
HIGH_INC_SMITH.visualization: Scraping the Chin: Position your body so the bar feels like it will scrape your chin.
HIGH_INC_SMITH.proTip: The Smith machine allows you to safely push the upper pecs to failure without stabilizers giving out.

MACH_LATERAL.name: Machine Lateral Raise
technique: Place elbows against pads
Drive elbows up/out leading the movement
Lower with a 3s eccentric
MACH_LATERAL.visualization: Puppet Strings: Strings are pulling your elbows to the ceiling. Hands are just hooks.
MACH_LATERAL.proTip: Keep traps relaxed. Machines remove the altered moment arm of free weights.

LEG_EXTENSION.name: Leg Extension
technique: Align knee joint with machine pivot
Dorsiflex ankles (pull toes toward shins)
Hold for 1s at peak
LEG_EXTENSION.visualization: The Glue Cue: Imagine your butt is super-glued to the seat.
LEG_EXTENSION.proTip: Dorsiflexing the toes reduces calf involvement and increases rectus femoris activation.

CABLE_OH_EXT.name: Overhead Cable Extension
technique: Set pulley at hip height
Keep elbows near ears
Extend arms overhead, separating rope
CABLE_OH_EXT.visualization: Throwing the Ball: Visualize throwing a heavy medicine ball over your head.
CABLE_OH_EXT.proTip: The money is in the stretch—let the rope pull your hands deep behind your neck.

RDL_BARBELL.name: Romanian Deadlift
technique: Unlock knees slightly
Hinge exclusively at hips
Stop when hips stop moving back
RDL_BARBELL.visualization: Car Door: Close a car door behind you using only your glutes.
RDL_BARBELL.proTip: The moment your hips stop traveling backward, the rep is over.

NEUTRAL_PULLUP.name: Weighted Pull-Up
technique: Use a neutral grip
Depress shoulders before pulling
Control the lowering phase
mistakes: Not going to a full hang
NEUTRAL_PULLUP.visualization: Elbows to Pockets: Drive elbows down into your back pockets.
NEUTRAL_PULLUP.proTip: Neutral grip biases the lats and brachialis while being safer on the shoulders.

CS_ROW.name: Chest-Supported Row
technique: Glue chest to pad
Protract shoulders at bottom
Retract and squeeze at top
CS_ROW.visualization: Wrap Around Pad: Feel your back wrapping around the pad at the bottom.
CS_ROW.proTip: Unlike pull-ups, we want the shoulder blades to move dynamically here.

SEATED_L_CURL.name: Seated Leg Curl
technique: Lock thigh pad down hard
Drive heels back and under
Control the 3s eccentric
SEATED_L_CURL.visualization: Digging a Trench: Dig into the ground with your heels.
SEATED_L_CURL.proTip: Seated curls place hamstrings in a lengthened position, superior to lying curls.

REV_PEC_DECK.name: Reverse Pec Deck
technique: Adjust handles to shoulder height
Keep arms rigid
Stop when arms align with body
REV_PEC_DECK.visualization: Pushing Walls Away: Push the walls away with the backs of your hands.
REV_PEC_DECK.proTip: Keep shoulder blades protracted. If you retract, traps take over.

INC_DB_CURL.name: Incline DB Curls
technique: Set bench to 45-60°
Keep elbows pointing at floor
Supinate at the top
INC_DB_CURL.visualization: Elbows in Cement: They can hinge, but cannot move forward.
INC_DB_CURL.proTip: Targets the long head via the stretch. Don't cut the bottom short.

HACK_SQUAT.name: Hack Squat
technique: Place feet low and shoulder-width on the platform
Unlock safeties and descend with a 3s eccentric
Drive through the whole foot, stopping just short of lockout
mistakes: Placing feet too high (shifts to glutes)
HACK_SQUAT.visualization: Elevator Shaft: Your torso rides straight down like an elevator — no forward lean.
HACK_SQUAT.proTip: The fixed plane lets you safely load the quads without spinal compression.

LEG_PRESS.name: Leg Press
technique: Place feet low and shoulder-width on the sled
Lower until knees reach 90°
Press through midfoot without locking out
mistakes: Letting hips curl off the pad at the bottom
LEG_PRESS.visualization: Push the World Away: You're not moving the sled — you're pushing the earth away with your legs.
LEG_PRESS.proTip: Low foot placement biases quads. Keep your lower back pinned to the pad at all times.

INC_MACH_PR.name: Incline Machine Press
technique: Adjust seat so handles align with upper chest
Press up while keeping scapula retracted
Control the negative with a 3s eccentric
mistakes: Letting shoulders roll forward at full extension
Using too much front delt by flaring elbows
INC_MACH_PR.visualization: Hug the Ceiling: Press up and slightly inward like you're hugging something overhead.
INC_MACH_PR.proTip: Machines stabilize the path so you can push to true muscular failure safely.

CABLE_LATERAL.name: Cable Lateral Raise
technique: Stand sideways to a low pulley
Lead with the elbow, arm slightly bent
Raise until arm is parallel to floor, then lower with control
mistakes: Raising above shoulder height (traps take over)
CABLE_LATERAL.visualization: Pouring Water: At the top, tilt your hand like you're pouring water from a jug.
CABLE_LATERAL.proTip: The cable provides constant tension throughout the ROM — no dead spot at the bottom.

DB_LATERAL.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
technique: Hold dumbbells at sides with a slight bend in elbows
Raise arms out to the sides leading with elbows
Pause at shoulder height, lower with 3s control
DB_LATERAL.visualization: Scarecrow Arms: Imagine strings pulling your elbows straight out to the sides.
DB_LATERAL.proTip: Slightly lean forward 10-15° to better align with the lateral delt fibers.

DB_RDL.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
technique: Hold dumbbells in front of thighs
Hinge at hips, sliding weights down the legs
Stop when you feel a deep hamstring stretch
mistakes: Bending knees too much (turning it into a squat)
DB_RDL.visualization: Drinking Bird: Your body tips forward from the hips like a drinking bird toy — rigid torso.
DB_RDL.proTip: Dumbbells allow a more natural hand path and subtle external rotation.

SMITH_RDL.name: Smith Machine RDL
technique: Stand with bar at hip crease, feet hip-width
Hinge back keeping the bar on the legs
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
mistakes: Standing too far from the bar path
Letting the bar drift away from legs
SMITH_RDL.visualization: Iron Rail: The bar moves on a rail — your body hinges around it like a gate.
SMITH_RDL.proTip: The fixed path lets you focus purely on the hip hinge without balance demands.

LAT_PULLDOWN.name: Lat Pulldown
technique: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Pull to upper chest, leaning back 15°
Squeeze lats at the bottom, extend fully at top
mistakes: Using biceps to yank the weight down
LAT_PULLDOWN.visualization: Bend the Bar: Try to bend the bar around your collarbone as you pull.
LAT_PULLDOWN.proTip: Full scapular elevation at the top maximizes the stretch on the lats.

SEATED_OHP.name: Seated OHP
technique: Set bench to 75-80° (not fully 90°)
Lower bar/handles to chin level
Press vertically, finishing with biceps by ears
Control the descent
mistakes: Arching back into a chest press
SEATED_OHP.visualization: Head Through Window: As you press up, push your head slightly forward 'through the window' created by your arms.
SEATED_OHP.proTip: Using a machine or Smith here is preferred over free weights for hypertrophy, allowing you to grind to failure safely.

TRI_PUSHDOWN.name: Triceps Pushdown
technique: Pin elbows to your ribcage
Hinge only at the elbow
Pull the rope apart at the bottom
Squeeze triceps hard
mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward / leaning on the rope
Moving the elbows forward and back
TRI_PUSHDOWN.visualization: Breaking the Rope: Visualize trying to rip the rope in half as you reach the bottom.
TRI_PUSHDOWN.proTip: Targets the lateral and medial heads of the triceps. Keep the tempo strict.

WIDE_CABLE_ROW.name: Wide Grip Cable Row
technique: Use a wide mag-grip or straight bar
Keep torso upright
Pull elbows high and wide (shoulder height)
Squeeze scapula together
WIDE_CABLE_ROW.visualization: Scarecrow Pull: Pull your elbows apart like a scarecrow. The goal is width.
WIDE_CABLE_ROW.proTip: By flaring the elbows out to 45-60 degrees, you bias the upper back rather than the lats.

FACE_PULL.name: Face Pulls
technique: Set rope to upper chest height
Grasp rope with thumbs facing back
Pull towards forehead while spreading hands
Externally rotate
FACE_PULL.visualization: Double Bicep Pose: Finish the movement in a 'double bicep' pose. Your knuckles should face the wall behind you.
FACE_PULL.proTip: This is not a heavy strength movement. It's for rotator cuff health and rear delts.

PREACHER_CURL.name: Preacher Curl
technique: Adjust seat so armpit fits snugly over pad
Extend arm fully
Curl weight without moving the upper arm
Squeeze biceps at the top
PREACHER_CURL.visualization: The Hinge: Your arm is a simple hinge. Nothing else in the body moves.
PREACHER_CURL.proTip: Exercises the biceps in the 'shortened position'. Control the negative to avoid tendon strain at full extension.
